posts.title: Benchmarks in the Age of Agents: The Memory-Bandwidth Sanity Check
posts.description: Give an AI agent a benchmark and it will optimize the number, sometimes past what the hardware allows. A two-line division, bytes touched over memory bandwidth, tells you which speedups to question. I ran it on a 22x database claim and on my own Ferrite numbers.

posts.title: io_uring vs epoll, Measured: What Completion I/O Actually Buys an HTTP Server
posts.description: Same Rust HTTP server, same binary, two kernel I/O backends. I ran the campaigns on my homelab, caught my own machine lying by 2.7x, and found out what thread-per-core and completion I/O really cost and really pay.

posts.title: Rigidity of Pattern-Avoiding Breadth-First Reading Words of Increasing Trees
posts.description: We study permutations obtained by reading increasing ordered trees in breadth-first order. For every integer k >= 2, a 312-avoiding permutation is realizable on a tree of maximum outdegree k if and only if it is realizable on the complete k-ary heap shape. A 231-avoiding permutation of length congruent to 1 modulo k is realizable with maximum outdegree k if and only if it is realizable on a full k
